newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares close bourse down from record high.
newsitem.headline: German shares close bourse down from record high.

text.p: German blue-chip shares, coming off an all-time high reached on Tuesday, closed down 0.72 percent as some investors turned to profit-taking in a quiet bourse trading session on Wednesday.
The DAX index, which reached a record close of 2,886.98 points on Tuesday, fell 20.91 points to end at 2,866.07 points, showing little movement during the day after shares tumbled in early trade.
"It's consolidation today," said one traderin Frankfurt.
Dealers said losses on Wall Street overnight and the dollar coming off 23-month highs reached on Tuesday had both weighed on the market.

The dollar, a major factor in the price of German exports, edged lower after German economic growth in the third quarter exceeded most expectations. Year-on-year gross domestic product growth doubled to 2.4 percent in the third quarter.
Trading followed the downward course set on Wall Street yesterday, when the Dow Jones index suffered its largest single-day setback since July. The Dow on Tuesday closed down 79.07 points at 6442.69.

Dealers said although the 2,900 point level on the DAX, breached in late computer trade on Tuesday looked out of reach in the short-term, prospects for a continued rally up to 3,000 points was still intact.
Pharmaceuticals group Schering AG and car maker Volkswagen AG led the way among the day's few gainers.
Schering rose more than 3.2 percent to close at 132.95 marks, continuing an steep ascent that began last Tuesday when it traded at 120.20.
The stock reached a record high of 134.90 marks in Wedensday's bourse session before paring gains.

Volkswagen climbed six marks to 598.50. The company's shares are seen as a buy opportunity below 600 marks, traders said. The stock has been under pressure since suffering a string of setbacks in its legal battle with U.S. giant General Motors Corp.
BMW AG, BASF AG and Hoechst AG all lost ground in electronic trading as a dip in the dollar below 1.56 marks scared investors away from export-dependent shares.

In early IBIS trading on Wednesday, BMW fell from highs reached in a late rally on Tuesday when the stock touched a record high of 1,076 points. But in bourse trade BMW ended up slightly, 50 pfennigs higher at 1,048 marks.
Chemicals group BASF finished bourse trading down 85 pfennigs at 59.15 marks. Hoechst, a drug maker, ended at 68.50 marks, down 70 pfennigs.
